title: fix(usage): coalesce incremental projection refreshes
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes excessive SQLite work on ordinary chat turns after proactive Usage projections were introduced in #169660. Every transcript publication could acquire and release a durable refresh lock and rescan transcript pages even when no Usage report was open.

## User Impact

Usage projections remain proactive, and an overview read flushes pending publication work so completed turn usage is immediately available. Startup backfills retain their existing nonblocking partial-report behavior. No configuration, schema, retention, or update migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing usage owner now coalesces publications for 100 ms, skips explicit user/metadata-only publications, and resumes SQLite scans after the previous sequence. It reads the transcript owner's existing rewrite watermark once; rewrites, rewinds, and branch changes rebuild visible ancestry. Each payload page is decoded once and retained only as navigation and small usage contributions.

Cache refresh exclusion belongs to the Gateway process. A process-local reservation replaces lock discovery/acquire/release SQL; the writer atomically upserts the checkpoint and changed month partitions. Incognito keeps its separate compute-owned locking. Usage-only writes continue to publish no session-fact invalidations. The unused lock-status worker API is deleted.

Removed checks and accepted edges:

- Durable lock PID/nonce discovery and release recovery: unsupported simultaneous foreign cache writers are not coordinated; the Gateway owns the database.
- Previous-envelope compare-and-swap: one refresh reservation owns these derived writes; explicit deletion still drains the retained writer.
- Repeated anchor, navigation/payload, post-scan metadata, and tail rereads: a concurrent rewrite may briefly leave a stale derived projection; its next publication rebuilds it using the existing rewrite watermark.
- Full-cache pruning on an incremental refresh: deletion/topology and full discovery retain pruning ownership.

## Evidence

- Area T1 inventory: **0 → 0**; the optimization reduces worker statements and requests.
- Regression coverage: suffix-only reads, totals against full scans after appends/rewrites/rewinds/compaction, immediate overview freshness, write exclusion, atomic partitions, deletion drainage, and actor residency.
- Codex autoreview: two rounds; one missing collection-access argument fixed, final review clean through P2. Changed-file oxfmt, type-aware oxlint, and `git diff --check` pass.
- PR CI supplies focused tests and type/lint/Madge/T1/dialect checks; the Knip export scan runs separately under the CPU gate.
- Live baseline/candidate pair passed: all 13 turns, child, cron, control-plane RPCs, compaction, and graceful shutdown. **Usage: 122 → 10 SQL / 18 → 2 requests per warmed turn**, below the 15/3 target. All five shared read families also decreased.
- LOC: +531 / −892 (net −361).

### Live statement and request measurements

Both runs use the same workload and instrumentation.

Live durations were 107.7s / 127.1s (ratio 1.18). Initial host 1-minute loads were 60.86 / 63.51. These are execution counts on a loaded host, not latency benchmarks. Both complete fixtures passed the 13 top-level turns, awaited child, control-plane RPCs, cron, committed compaction, and graceful shutdown. Calibration passed independently on MAIN and worker: 8 calls, 2 prepares, 7 successful statements, zero failures.

Usage work decreases in every exercised phase: connect 49→22 SQL, first turn 117→9, second session 357→38, cron 77→9, and compaction 40→6. The six usage families sum to 1,864→184 SQL and 280→38 requests across the whole workload.

The larger raw connect window reflects an existing 689-statement database `open` admission moving from boot; combined boot+connect falls 3,225→2,983 SQL. The larger compaction/shutdown windows contain deferred Memory admission and synchronization: `schema.admit` contributes 135 direct + 133 domain-publication statements, followed by source/vector/cache work. Their source stacks are the unchanged `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-publication.worker.ts`, `manager-source-index-kernel.ts`, and `manager-embedding-cache.ts`. They do not add usage work, and the full workload decreases by 2,164 statements and 407 requests.


### CI diagnosis and final proof

Initial CI at `580dd4173031` passed production and test typechecks, source contracts/export collisions, Madge (zero cycles), and database worker/dialect/test-mock ratchets. Two Usage test fixtures depended on the removed lock-write side effects: rollback injection now explicitly admits the writer before adding its trigger; the failure/recovery fixture shuts down a cache-miss worker through the runtime owner. Commit `f4d43500106a` changes only those tests, so the measured production inputs remain unchanged. The rollback file passes 17/17 locally (`pnpm test src/infra/session-cost-usage-cache.sqlite.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, 116.47s command / 106.95s Vitest; 9% test time, dominated by compiler startup). The worker file passes 9/9 (`pnpm test src/infra/session-cost-usage-cache.worker.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, 119.55s command / 102.29s Vitest).

Initial-run inherited failures (the final-head lint jobs now pass):

- `check-lint-core-1`: `users-github.test.ts:679:40`, `typescript(no-unnecessary-type-arguments)`. The unchanged main file has blob `c1c09082fa2438b05c6ae522290d013b035cc143`; exact rule/line reproduced by type-aware oxlint on main. [PR job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38269608825/job/114881191099).
- `session-accessor.pending-inputs.test.ts`, “stages repeated relocation through savepoints and restores it on rollback”: `database is locked` at `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`. Exact test/error reproduced on current main `f6dd2d3d` (1/29 failed, 308.52s command / 284.08s Vitest); candidate `580dd417` passed 29/29 (284.86s / 268.45s). The test, transaction/admission and transcript-reconcile sources are byte-identical. This fixture mixes synchronous transactions with background projection writes; no repair is claimed. [PR job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38269608825/job/114880908541).

The incremental append/rewrite/rewind/compaction regressions passed CI (worker-refresh and projection shard: 0.757s total; individual new cases 0–1ms). Initial cache SQLite and cache worker shards took 91.32s and 68.28s respectively; these include other files and the now-corrected fixture failures. No SDK or update-cell scope.

The final export cleanup (`adfdc968aabb`) removes the obsolete single-transcript resolver, uses the batched resolver in test support, and makes the existing incognito lock imports explicit so Knip can follow their production consumers. It changes no SQL or refresh scheduling. The live measurement remains applicable.

Final-head Knip export scans pass with zero production, full-tree, and script findings (`pnpm deadcode:exports`); changed-file type-aware lint, formatting, and diff checks pass.

Final head `adfdc968aabb` passes all production/test typecheck shards, core and extension lint, source contracts/export collisions, architecture/Madge, and database worker/dialect/test-mock ratchets in [CI run 38271965137](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38271965137). The sole failed test shard repeats the independently reproduced main pending-inputs lock failure ([final-head job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38271965137/job/114889323849)); landing uses the authorized inherited-failure exception. CI has completed: `checks-node-changed-compact-small-15` and `build-artifacts` also passed. The only failed test is the inherited pending-inputs savepoint case above; the aggregate CI gate is red for that same failure. All other scheduled jobs passed or were skipped by their workflow conditions.
